players.product: medium-voltage switchgear, power control rooms / electrical houses and Remsdaq automation controllers for data-center utility connection (38 kV) and behind-the-meter on-site generation power islands

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 results (CFO Mike Metcalf): total revenue $297 million vs $279 million, 6% higher YoY; gross margin 29.6% (lower by 30 basis points YoY, 120 basis points higher sequentially, favorable project closeouts roughly 90 basis points of tailwind); net income $45.9 million or $1.25 per diluted share. By market, commercial and other industrial revenue +35% YoY, electric utility +14%, oil and gas +11%, petrochemical -37%. International revenue up $14 million to $64 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $297 million (+6%); gross margin 29.6%; $1.25 per diluted share; commercial and other industrial +35%

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog: Q2 new orders $490 million, 'nearly double' the year-ago quarter, bringing the mid-year total to nearly $1 billion; book-to-bill 1.7 times for both Q2 and the first half. Two mega orders each exceeding $75 million: 'the largest utility order that the business has ever recorded' for a large generation facility in the Eastern U.S., and a medium voltage electrical distribution order destined for a data center in the central U.S. Backlog $1.8 billion, a 33% increase ($438 million) YoY and $189 million higher sequentially; CEO Brett Cope says backlog 'now provides visibility well into our fiscal 2028'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 orders $490 million; book-to-bill 1.7 times; backlog $1.8 billion (+33%, +$438 million YoY, +$189 million QoQ); two mega orders each over $75 million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog mix at Q2: roughly 5% petrochem, 29% oil and gas, 30% utility, 6% traction, 29% commercial and other industrial - and data center is 'in the low 20s of that 29'. Cope traces the data-center share of backlog from 7% a couple of years ago to 15, then 22, 'and now, you know, jumping next couple quarters' (the $400 million+ April order is not yet in Q2 backlog).
quarterly_data.figure: commercial and other industrial 29% of backlog, of which data center in the low 20s; data-center share history 7% -> 15 -> 22

quarterly_data.signal: FIRST DISCLOSURE OF THE RECORD DATA-CENTER ORDER: in early April (after Q2 close) Powell won a mega project for the first phase of a new greenfield data center - a behind-the-meter design for a planned multi-phased campus, 'in excess of $400 million', 'the largest project award in Powell's history', booked in fiscal Q3. Cope: the customer 'is in the neo-cloud space'; the scope is 'all outside the data center', 'a couple of gigawatts initial phase', 'One purchase order' (not split). Content: 'A mix of voltages, quite a bit of 15 kV, a lot of 38, both primary switchgear as well as secondary switches', touching 'just about every division' in North America. Burn: 'roughly a 2-year burn. It'll run through the end of fiscal 2028' / 'a two and a half year build out'. Cope hopes to 'get a shot at the internal side of the data center' and at later phases (no guarantee).
quarterly_data.figure: data-center order in excess of $400 million (neo-cloud, behind-the-meter, a couple of gigawatts initial phase), runs through the end of fiscal 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Behind-the-meter raises Powell's addressable market: Cope says behind-the-meter designs are 'akin to a power island' with 'a higher degree of complexity around the gear' and 'around the automation', so 'the TAM on a behind-the-meter is going up for Powell, beyond a straight utility connect'. Route to market is widening from indirect OEM/partner channels to direct conversations 'with the contractor or even the ultimate end client'; early signs of 'a nice engineering efficiency on these large jobs in the data center market'; Remsdaq resources added in the U.S. with 'synergistic adds' in the data center market.

Capacity plan: evaluating a lease of approximately 50,000 square feet near the Moseley campus to support a new $8 million investment in fabrication equipment; still assessing a larger facility needing $70 million-$100 million of capital for an additional 250,000-300,000 square feet, with a decision 'within the next few quarters' (board meeting in a couple of weeks). A greenfield would take 'conservatively two years'; a bridging lease could give productive capacity 'within 6 months'; such a facility 'can run $100 million-$250 million' of revenue. Jacintoport expansion (335,000 sq ft) on schedule, with most of the $12 million-$13 million yard upgrade in 2H FY2026; second satellite engineering center leased in the Houston Metro area.
quarterly_data.figure: $8 million fab equipment; $70 million-$100 million facility option for 250,000-300,000 square feet, $100 million-$250 million revenue capacity; Jacintoport $12 million-$13 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity-constrained demand: asked whether Powell has turned down orders, Cope says 'I wouldn't say we're turning anything down. Are we able to meet the schedules of everything coming in the door? The answer to that is no.' For another job the size of the $400 million+ order, 'the constraints would be people and supply chain'. Pricing: 'In certain product areas that have become constrained in the demand supply curve, we are absolutely moving up price incrementally'. Copper exposure is covered by a hedging program that 'acts as an insurance policy to protect margins that we have in backlog'. Cope also cites the White House Section 303 Defense Production Act determination designating substations and switchgear as essential to national defense.

Balance sheet and spending: Q2 operating cash flow $51 million; PP&E investment $1.8 million; cash and short-term investments $545 million at March 31st, 2026, no debt. R&D about 1.4% of revenues, expected to hold 'between 1 and 1.5%'; SG&A 8.7% of revenue. 3-for-1 forward stock split effective April 2, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: cash $545 million, no debt; operating cash flow $51 million; R&D about 1.4% of revenues
